judgments.reasoning_cat1: It combines a class-arbitration bar, a carve-out reserving the waiver's 'validity, effect, and enforceability' to a court 'notwithstanding any other provision herein', and a conditional fallback to court litigation — a dense set of operative directions whose interaction is genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The court-only reservation directly cuts against Paragraph 1(a) (c017), which sends the validity and scope of the Arbitration Provision to the arbitrator, and its 'proceed in court' fallback must be squared with Paragraph 8's (c026) rule that the entire provision is void in that event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Upon the election by you, us, or Lender, any dispute shall be resolved by binding arbitration' mixes permissive election with mandatory command, and 'any other arbitrator ... reasonably satisfactory to us' plus the CAB's right to pick if the customer does not choose within 20 days leaves the selection mechanism one-sided and open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its fee-advance cap of $1000 sits against Paragraph 5 (c023), which promises to advance the customer's whole portion of the Arbitration Fees including arbitrator's fees without a cap, and its 30-day remedy notice overlaps the 60-day pre-suit notice in c011.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The fee-shifting sentences are detailed and internally consistent, though 'does not render a decision or an award in your favor' is a soft trigger for reimbursement in a partial-victory case.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 4 (c022) limits the CAB's advance of arbitration fees to $1000 and to filing, administrative and hearing fees, while this paragraph promises to advance the customer's portion including arbitrator's fees without limit — a direct conflict within the same arbitration provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any dispute which cannot be adjudicated within the jurisdiction of a small claims tribunal' is an uncertain boundary — it could mean amount-in-controversy, subject matter, or the availability of class relief — and it decides which forum applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes arbitration automatic for disputes outside small-claims jurisdiction, whereas Paragraph 4 (c022) makes arbitration depend on a party's election, and Paragraph 3 (c021) opens with 'Except as provided in Paragraph 6' without saying how the two interlock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional two-sentence choice-of-law rule with a clear fallback trigger; nothing in it is genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches GOVERNING LAW (c028), which carves the arbitration provision out of Texas law in favour of the FAA, and the interstate-commerce stipulation in c013.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The survival and severability sentences are clear on their face, but the 'blow-up' proviso — the whole provision is void if the class waiver is invalid — depends on the contestable phrase 'deemed invalid or unenforceable' and by whom.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ENTIRE AGREEMENT (c031) says an invalid provision 'shall be reformed if practicable' and 'shall not in any way affect the remaining provisions', which is the opposite result to the void-the-whole-clause rule stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly mangled at the key operative points ('You may choose, f fo opt-out', 'notify us inf' 'ng within nincty (90) calendar days'), and the address line is duplicated and garbled, obscuring how a valid opt-out is made.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A ninety-day opt-out window runs well past the three-day cancellation right (c033/c034) and past the loan's first payments, and c009's reference to 'rejecting' the arbitration agreement uses different language for the same mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence choosing Texas law with an express FAA carve-out; its terms are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the arbitration provision 'is governed by' the FAA full stop, while Paragraph 7 (c025) contemplates Texas arbitration law if the FAA is held inapplicable — a gap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutorily prescribed warning in capitals; it imposes no obligation and has nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It advises against 'repeated or frequent use' while the opt-out clause (c027) contemplates successive transactions, but no operative term is contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Regulator contact details only; purely informational.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the arbitration provision or the pre-suit notice clause (c011) purports to bar an administrative complaint, so no tension arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Relating to the subject matter of this Agreement' is an imprecise integration boundary in a transaction that also involves a separate lender note and disclosure statement, and the reform-if-practicable rule is itself open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its severance-and-reform rule cannot be squared with Arbitration Paragraph 8 (c026), which voids the entire arbitration provision if the class waiver falls, and its integration language sits against c017's reference to 'this Disclosure Statement' and c032's separate documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acknowledgment list is so corrupted ('A SEPARATE If T; 2) THIS ZES AGREEMENT') that the documents the customer is certifying receipt of cannot be identified from the text itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It certifies receipt of a separate document and of two Notices of Cancellation, which ties back to c033 and the two attached notices, and it confirms assent to the arbitration provision that c027 lets the customer opt out of for ninety days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Before midnight of the third day after the date of the transaction' fixes a deadline by reference to 'the date of the transaction', an event this Agreement never defines and which need not be the date of signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Notice of Cancellation (c034) measures the same right as 'within three days after the date the contract is signed', and the executed date (4/9/2012) versus the printed deadline (04/12/2012) supplies a third measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within three days after the date the contract is signed' is a workable formula but 'without any penalty or obligation' sits oddly with a transaction whose fee is financed into a third-party loan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the cancellation window differently from the body NOTICE (c033), which runs to midnight of the third day after 'the date of the transaction', and the LOC revocation in c006 turns on which of the two applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with a definite trigger and period; the only softness is that 'any payment made by you under this contract' may or may not reach sums paid to the lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the CAB fee is financed into the lender's loan (c004), what a customer has 'made ... under this contract' to be returned is not obvious, but no provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Mail or deliver ... not later than midnight on 04/12/2012' leaves it uncertain whether a mailed notice must be posted or received by that time, though the fixed date otherwise makes the deadline concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fixed 04/12/2012 date is consistent with a 4/9/2012 execution and with c033/c034, and c035 assumes receipt by the seller as the trigger for refund, which is in some tension with a mailing-based deadline.
